findings.issue: 鳴らせ is the imperative (命令形) of transitive 鳴らす plus emphatic particle よ — exactly the analysis sibling sentence 186677 gives. It is not stem + causative せ 'used as a command'; a bare causative stem cannot function as an imperative.

findings.fix: 鳴らせ is the imperative form of the transitive verb 鳴らす ('to ring/sound'); final よ reinforces the command
notes: Bare causative stem 鳴らせ- is not a command (causative imperative = 鳴らせろ/鳴らせよ). Correct parse: imperative of 鳴らす + particle よ, exactly as sibling 186677 states.

findings.issue: Counter 杯 after いっ is read ぱい (h→p after sokuon): いっぱい. Reading ばい is wrong in this context (that is the 倍 'times/fold' pattern).
findings.current: ばい

findings.fix: ぱい

杯 after sokuon is ぱい (h→p); ばい here is simply wrong.

findings.issue: Romaji carries the same wrong reading: ichibai should be ippai (コップ１杯 = koppu ippai).
findings.current: koppuichibainomizuokudasai.

findings.issue: 六階 is standardly read ろっかい (6 geminates before k-row counters: 六回/六階 = ろっかい, taught in all JLPT floor-counter lists), not ろくかい.
findings.current: このえれべーたーわろくかいよりうえにわいけません。
findings.suggested: このえれべーたーわろっかいよりうえにわいけません。
findings.fix: このえれべーたーわろっかいよりうえにわいけません。
notes: 六階 is standardly ろっかい; ろくかい is a nonstandard variant no floor-counter list teaches.
六 geminates before the k-row counter 階: ろっかい is the standard taught reading; ろくかい is marginal for a learner corpus.

findings.issue: 六 in 六階 is realized ろっ (gemination), not ろく; token readings in this corpus use surface phonetics (かい stays on the 階 token).
findings.current: ろく
findings.suggested: ろっ
findings.fix: ろっ
notes: Surface-phonetic token convention: 六 before 階 realizes as ろっ, with かい on the 階 token.
Token readings are surface-phonetic in this corpus, so 六 must be ろっ once kana is ろっかい.

findings.issue: Romaji carries the same wrong reading: rokukai should be rokkai (六階 = rokkai).

findings.issue: "faço-em" is ungrammatical and attaches the に gloss to the wrong word: に follows コート, so the corpus's hyphen convention (cf. "Aqui-para vir") requires "casaco-em". Current text misrepresents the structure the lit field is meant to teach.
findings.current: Este casaco, faço-em (escolho) (viu.)
findings.suggested: Este casaco-em faço (= escolho), viu.
findings.fix: Este casaco-em faço (= escolho), viu.

"faço-em" is not Portuguese and mis-attaches に to する; the stray "(viu.)" parenthetical is also malformed.

findings.issue: English drops ここの entirely ("the university students here"); pt and lit_en keep it, so en is the odd one out and loses the locational anchor.
findings.current: The students are for the most part diligent.

en is the source Tatoeba human translation (Layer A); its looseness is inherited, and pt/lit_en already carry ここの.

findings.issue: Compound ケーキ作り takes rendaku and is read けーきづくり (kēki-ZUkuri), as in パン作り/手作り/お菓子作り; つくり is the wrong reading in this compound.
findings.current: けーきつくりにしっぱいした。
findings.suggested: けーきづくりにしっぱいした。
findings.fix: けーきづくりにしっぱいした。
notes: N+作り compounds rendaku (手作り/パン作り/ものづくり); けーきつくり is a tokenizer artifact, reading is けーきづくり.
X作り compounds rendaku (手作り てづくり, パンづくり, ケーキづくり); づくり is the correct in-context reading, つくり is wrong.

findings.issue: Token 作り as second element of the compound ケーキ作り undergoes rendaku: reading is づくり, not つくり.
findings.current: つくり
findings.suggested: づくり
findings.fix: づくり
notes: As the second element of ケーキ作り, 作り is read づくり; standalone つくり is the dictionary-form artifact.
Same rendaku: as second element of ケーキ作り the token reads づくり; Lyman's Law does not block it.

findings.issue: Same rendaku error as kana: ke-kitsukuri should be ke-kizukuri (ケーキ作り = kēkizukuri).
findings.current: ke-kitsukurinishippaishita.
findings.suggested: ke-kizukurinishippaishita.
findings.fix: ke-kizukurinishippaishita.

Follows from the kana fix; ke-kizukuri matches the file's Hepburn/ー='-' convention. Not the known punctuation issue.

findings.issue: ケーキ means 'cake', not 'pie' (pie = パイ); lit_pt correctly says 'O bolo'. The literal English introduces a wrong noun.
findings.current: The pie, once you finish eating it, doesn't stay on your hands.
findings.suggested: The cake, once you finish eating it, doesn't stay on your hands.
findings.fix: The cake, once you finish eating it, doesn't stay on your hands.

ケーキ = cake (pie = パイ); lit_pt already says 'O bolo' and en/pt say cake. 'The pie' is a wrong noun.

findings.issue: Gloss lists 'pie' as a sense of ケーキ; ケーキ never means pie (that is パイ). Wrong-sense gloss misleads learners.
findings.current: pie, cake
findings.suggested: cake
findings.fix: cake
notes: JMdict ケーキ = cake only; 'pie' is a spurious leading sense that misteaches the word.
JMdict ケーキ = 'cake' only; leading a learner gloss with the wrong sense 'pie' misteaches the word.

findings.issue: Gloss lists 'torta' as a sense of ケーキ; ケーキ é 'bolo', não 'torta' (torta = パイ/タルト). Wrong-sense gloss.
findings.current: torta, bolo
findings.suggested: bolo
findings.fix: bolo
notes: ケーキ = bolo; torta corresponds to パイ/タルト. Wrong sense listed first.
ケーキ = bolo; 'torta' (パイ/タルト) is a wrong sense and it is listed first.

findings.issue: 立ち見 is a noun ('standing room / watching while standing'), not a future-tense verb; 'will stand' misrepresents the word class. lit_pt ('lugar-em-pé') and the token gloss are correct.
findings.current: Definitely / will stand / [emphasis].

findings.fix: Definitely / standing room / [emphasis].
notes: 立ち見 is a noun (standing room); 'will stand' misstates word class and contradicts lit_pt and the token gloss.
立ち見 is a noun; 'will stand' misstates word class and contradicts lit_pt ('lugar-em-pé') and the token gloss.

findings.issue: いく means 'to go', never 'to walk' (that is 歩く); the spurious first sense misteaches the verb. The contextual sense 'to turn out' is fine.
findings.current: to walk / to come out / to turn out (result)
findings.suggested: to go / to turn out (result)
findings.fix: to go / to turn out (result)
notes: 行く/いく = to go; 'to walk' is 歩く and is not a sense of いく. Leading gloss is wrong.
'to walk'/'to come out' are literalizations of the pt idioms andar/sair; in English they are wrong senses of いく and 'to go' is missing.

findings.issue: Quoted Japanese garbled: topic particle written before the pronoun ('は私たち'); should be 私たちは.
findings.current: The main clause は私たち...知った says "we found out."
findings.suggested: The main clause 私たちは...知った says "we found out."
findings.fix: The main clause 私たちは...知った says "we found out."
notes: 'は私たち' is impossible particle order; the quoted main clause is 私たちは…知った.
'は私たち' is ungrammatical particle placement quoted in a learner explanation; must be 私たちは.

findings.issue: Same garbled quote as expl_en: 'は私たち' should be 私たちは.
findings.current: A oração principal は私たち...知った diz "nós soubemos".
findings.suggested: A oração principal 私たちは...知った diz "nós soubemos".
findings.fix: A oração principal 私たちは...知った diz "nós soubemos".
notes: Same garbled quote; particle は cannot precede 私たち.
Same garbled quote as expl_en; particle は must follow 私たち.

findings.issue: Missing space/word makes 'The!' read as an interjection; the sentence refers to the exclamation mark.
findings.current: The! and the blunt imperative give a tone of order/irritation.
findings.suggested: The exclamation mark (!) and the blunt imperative give a tone of order/irritation.
findings.fix: The exclamation mark (!) and the blunt imperative give a tone of order/irritation.
notes: 'The!' reads as a broken fragment; the text means the exclamation mark. Real prose defect, not style.
Verified in file: bare ASCII '!' glued to 'The', no fullwidth quote or space — dangling article, broken sentence.

findings.issue: Mesmo problema do expl_en: 'O!' lê-se como interjeição; falta a palavra para o ponto de exclamação.

Verified 'O! e o imperativo bruto' — reads as interjection; noun for the exclamation mark is missing.

findings.issue: Genitive reversed: お茶の質 is 'the quality of the tea' (head = 質), but 'Quality tea' means high-grade tea, flipping modifier and head. Contradicts en/pt/expl and misteaches の structure in the structural-mirror field.
findings.current: Quality tea [topic] is in the process of going down.
findings.suggested: The quality of the tea [topic] is in the process of going down.
findings.fix: The quality of the tea [topic] is in the process of going down.
notes: Head/modifier flipped: お茶の質 = quality OF tea; 'Quality tea' reads as high-grade tea and contradicts en/expl_en.
お茶の質 head is 質; 'Quality tea' means high-grade tea, inverting modifier/head and contradicting en + expl.

findings.issue: Genitive reversed: 'Chá de qualidade' means 'quality (high-grade) tea', but お茶の質 is 'a qualidade do chá' (núcleo = 質). Sense-flipping in the structural field; contradicts pt and expl_pt.
findings.current: Chá de qualidade [tópico] descendo está-em-processo.
findings.suggested: A qualidade do chá [tópico] descendo está-em-processo.
findings.fix: A qualidade do chá [tópico] descendo está-em-processo.
notes: 'Chá de qualidade' = chá de alta qualidade; núcleo é 質, logo 'A qualidade do chá'. Contradiz pt e expl_pt.
'Chá de qualidade' = quality tea; correct is 'A qualidade do chá' (núcleo 質), matching pt and expl_pt.

findings.issue: Accent typo: verb form should be 'pratica' (praticar, 3rd sg.); 'prática' with accent is the noun/adjective.

findings.fix: Como é frase de cobertura, ela pratica から temporal + 〜ている
notes: Real orthographic error: verb form is 'pratica'; 'prática' is the noun/adjective.
Verb slot requires 'pratica'; 'prática' is the noun/adjective — orthographic error in learner-facing pt-BR.

findings.issue: Adds a clause not in the Japanese ('so don't worry') instead of mirroring the trailing から, unlike lit_pt which correctly ends with 'porque'. Inaccurate as a structural mirror.
findings.current: Mom will do anything for you, so don't worry.
findings.suggested: Mom, whatever it may be, will do (it for you), because— (reassuring から).
findings.fix: Mom, whatever it may be, will do (it for you), because— (reassuring から).
notes: Trailing から elides its consequent; 'so don't worry' matches expl_en's own framing and the batch's semi-free lit_en register.
'so don't worry' spells out the dangling から's reassurance implicature, which expl_en itself states; stylistic, not a sense change.

findings.issue: Subject mismatch: en renders a 3rd-person-plural subject while pt ('Graças a você, vou indo bem'), lit_en ('I'm (keeping) well') and both expl fields all treat the unexpressed subject as 1st person (default for humble しております). Internally inconsistent and misleading without context.
findings.current: They're all fine, thank you.
findings.suggested: I'm doing well, thank you.
findings.fix: I'm doing well, thank you.
notes: 3rd-plural 'They're all' has no basis in the JP (no plural referent) and contradicts pt, lit_en and both expl fields, which all read 1st person.
pt, lit_en, lit_pt and both expl all commit to 1st person; 'all' has no JP counterpart. Loose Tanaka pairing — same class as accepted 187583/187580 en fixes.

findings.issue: Archaic, opaque English ('got at bidding') is not a natural translation and invites misreading of 'bidding' as auction bidding; meaning is 'money can't be obtained that easily / on demand'.
findings.current: Money cannot be got at bidding.
findings.suggested: Money isn't something you can just get that easily.
findings.fix: Money isn't something you can just get that easily.
notes: 'at bidding' = 'at one's bidding/on command' — archaic but semantically correct; lit_en already gives the plain reading. Style only.
Archaic 'at bidding' (= at one's command) reads as auction bidding; same Tanaka-artifact class as the already-accepted 118746 'gets across me' fix.

findings.issue: Gloss suggests the tag-question use ('isn't it'), but here じゃ is part of plain negation じゃない = 'is not' (the expl itself stresses this is the genuine negating use; pt gloss 'não é' is correct).
findings.current: (part of 'isn't it')
findings.suggested: (part of 'is not')
findings.fix: (part of 'is not')
notes: 'isn't it' reads as a tag question; here じゃない is plain negation, as the pt gloss ('não é') and expl_en both state.
Defect real but mis-indexed: it is tokens[5].en (じゃ) that reads "(part of 'isn't it')"; tokens[6] (ない) already says 'is not'. Apply to じゃ.

findings.issue: Mismatched parentheses: full-width （ opened but closed with ASCII ), leaving a stray bracket in the learner-facing text.

Full-width （ closed by ASCII ) — objective typo in learner-facing text; ASCII parens after Japanese are the batch convention (cf. 227004, 227007).

findings.issue: Mismatched parentheses: full-width （ opened but closed with ASCII ), leaving a stray bracket in the learner-facing text.

notes: Same mismatched （...) bracket pair as expl_en; mechanical fix, no meaning change.
Same mismatched bracket pair as expl_en; objective typo, trivial fix, matches batch convention.

findings.issue: Terminology error: 当たり (あたり, three morae) is not a 'syllable'; it is the final element of the noun 八つ当たり. The pedagogical point (たり is word-internal, not the listing grammar) is right, but the wording is linguistically false.
findings.current: 八つ当たり (...) is a noun whose last syllable is 当たり
findings.suggested: 八つ当たり (...) is a noun that ends in 当たり
findings.fix: is a noun that ends in 当たり
notes: 当たり is three morae (あ-た-り), not a syllable; 'ends in 当たり' keeps the (correct) pedagogical point without the false label.
当たり = a-ta-ri (3 morae) is not a syllable; false phonological claim in pedagogical text. Anchor: quote the live clause, not the '(...)' ellipsis.

findings.issue: Terminology error: 当たり (あたり, três moras) não é uma 'sílaba'; é o elemento final do substantivo 八つ当たり. A afirmação pedagógica está certa, mas o rótulo linguístico é falso.
findings.current: é um substantivo cuja última sílaba é 当たり
findings.suggested: é um substantivo que termina em 当たり
findings.fix: é um substantivo que termina em 当たり
notes: 'última sílaba' is factually wrong for あたり (3 moras) and reads sloppy; 'que termina em 当たり' preserves the point.
'sílaba' is even more technical in pt-BR; 当たり is 3 morae/syllables. Wrong linguistic fact, pedagogical point preserved by the fix.

findings.issue: 一日中 in the 'all day long' sense is read いちにちじゅう (the duration suffix 中 voices to じゅう after time spans, as in 一年中・世界中); the kana transcribes it as いちにちちゅう, a wrong reading.
findings.current: うちのいぬわいちにちちゅうひなたによこになっている。
findings.suggested: うちのいぬわいちにちじゅうひなたによこになっている。
findings.fix: うちのいぬわいちにちじゅうひなたによこになっている。
notes: 一日中 is いちにちじゅう (duration 中 voices: 一年中/世界中); ちゅう is the 'in progress' suffix. Wrong in-context reading.
一日中 is いちにちじゅう (duration 中 voices, cf. 一年中/世界中). いちにちちゅう is a wrong in-context reading.

findings.issue: The suffix 中 'throughout' rendaku-voices after 一日: いちにちじゅう. ちゅう is the 'in the middle of doing' suffix (電話中, 会議中), not the reading in 一日中.
findings.current: ちゅう
findings.suggested: じゅう
findings.fix: じゅう
notes: tokens[6] is 中 in 一日中; reading must be じゅう, not the 電話中-type ちゅう.
Same defect at token level: 中 in 一日中 reads じゅう; ちゅう is the 'in progress' suffix (会議中).

findings.issue: Propagates the kana reading error: ichinichichuu should be ichinichijuu (一日中 = いちにちじゅう).
findings.current: uchinoinuwaichinichichuuhinataniyokoninatteiru.
findings.suggested: uchinoinuwaichinichijuuhinataniyokoninatteiru.
findings.fix: uchinoinuwaichinichijuuhinataniyokoninatteiru.
notes: Propagates the same reading error; 'juu' matches corpus romaji style (cf. juusho in 228648).
Propagation of the kana error; suggested ichinichijuu is correct and matches the fixed kana.

findings.issue: 横になっている is a resultant state ('está deitado'); 'está se tornando deitado' renders it as an ongoing change, contradicting expl_pt itself ('descreve um ESTADO contínuo') and lit_en ('it lies down').
findings.current: Quanto ao cachorro da nossa casa, o dia inteiro, ao sol, está se tornando deitado.
findings.suggested: Quanto ao cachorro da nossa casa, o dia inteiro, ao sol, fica deitado.
findings.fix: Quanto ao cachorro da nossa casa, o dia inteiro, ao sol, está deitado.
notes: なっている here is a resultant state; 'está se tornando' renders an ongoing change, contradicting lit_en ('it lies down') and expl_pt ('ESTADO contínuo').
なっている with change verb なる = resultant state; 'se tornando' reads as ongoing change, contradicting expl_pt and the いる token note ('está deitado').

findings.issue: As phrased, English parses the neighbor as the one who dislikes ('the person next door ... doesn't like very much'). With 〜が好きではない the が-phrase is the liked one (as expl_en correctly states); the mirror should predicate 'is not much liked' of the neighbor.
findings.current: As for the mother of the house (topic), the person next door (subject) doesn't like very much (negation).
findings.suggested: As for the mother of the house (topic), the person next door (subject) is not much liked (negation).
findings.fix: As for the mother of the house (topic), the person next door (subject) is not liked very much (negation).
notes: Gloss tags 隣の人 '(subject)' then predicates 'doesn't like' of it, reversing the が-argument structure the expl_en teaches for 好き.
Tagging 隣の人 '(subject)' then an active 'doesn't like' reverses the roles vs. the en field; passive keeps the が-mirror without the reversal.

findings.issue: Token list tiles the surface twice: fragment tokens ウスター (i=0) and ソース (i=1) carry all-null glosses and are immediately followed by the full compound ウスターソース (i=2) covering the same text. Any surface-tiling renderer duplicates the word.
findings.current: ウスター + ソース + ウスターソース (same surface tokenized twice)
findings.suggested: Delete tokens[0] ウスター and tokens[1] ソース; keep ウスターソース as the single glossed token.
findings.fix: Delete tokens[0] ウスター and tokens[1] ソース; keep ウスターソース as the single glossed token.
notes: ウスター+ソース+ウスターソース tiles the surface twice; no other item in the batch adds a compound token over its parts. Renderer would duplicate.
Concatenating tokens yields ウスターソースウスターソースが…; every other item tiles the surface exactly once. Deleting the two null-gloss fragments restores it.

findings.issue: The parenthetical '(right?)' glosses final の as a confirmation tag — that is ね, not の. Sentence-final の here is the casual/explanatory question particle (as expl_en itself states), and a wh-question cannot take 'right?'.
findings.current: When does it end? (right?)
findings.suggested: When is it that it ends?
findings.fix: When is it that it ends?
notes: '(right?)' glosses の as the tag ね; expl_en itself calls it the casual question particle, and a wh-question cannot take a confirmation tag.
'(right?)' glosses の as the tag ね; impossible with a wh-question. Suggested 'When is it that it ends?' matches the corpus's own のですか device (228648).

findings.issue: '(né?)' equates の with the tag ね ('não é?'); here の is the casual/explanatory question particle, so the gloss teaches the wrong particle mapping. Mirror it with 'é que' (the same device the corpus uses for のですか, cf. sent:tatoeba-228648).
findings.current: Quando termina(r)? (né?)
findings.suggested: Quando é que termina(r)?
findings.fix: Quando é que termina?
notes: Same wrong particle mapping ('né?' = ね). 'é que' is the corpus device (cf. 228648 lit_pt); drop the stray '(r)' since 終わる is non-past.
'(né?)' maps の onto ね (wrong particle). Fix as suggested but drop the stray '(r)' — 終わる is plain present/future, so 'termina' alone.

findings.issue: English word 'coverage' left untranslated in the pt-BR explanation; elsewhere in the corpus it is rendered 'cobertura' (cf. sent:tatoeba-228248).

findings.suggested: O foco aqui é cobertura (vocabulário e estrutura básica de pergunta/resposta)
findings.fix: O foco aqui é cobertura (vocabulário e estrutura básica de pergunta/resposta)

Untranslated English 'coverage' in learner-facing pt-BR; corpus renders it 'cobertura' elsewhere (228248). Recurs in 6 batch files.

findings.issue: 'neighborhood' is 近所, not 隣; in 隣の人 the word means 'next door / adjacent'. 'side / neighborhood' does not fit this context.
findings.current: side / neighborhood
findings.suggested: next door / adjacent
findings.fix: next door / adjacent
notes: JMdict glosses 隣 as 'next to/adjoining/neighbour'; 'side' is accurate and 'neighborhood' is loose but not sense-changing — 人's gloss already says 'the neighbor'.
'neighborhood' is 近所; 隣 is 'next to / adjoining' and no standard entry lists 'neighborhood'. Wrong sense for 隣の人.

findings.issue: 'vizinhança' (= 近所) is the wrong sense for 隣, which in 隣の人 means 'do lado / da casa ao lado'.
findings.current: lado / vizinhança
findings.suggested: do lado / vizinho(a) (da casa ao lado)

findings.issue: でございます is 丁寧語 (polite/formal copula), not humble (謙譲語) — here it does not lower the speaker at all. Also inconsistent with expl_pt, which correctly says only 'forma extra-polida' with no humble claim.

ございます is 丁寧語, not 謙譲語 — it is freely used of the listener's things (お荷物はこちらでございます); 'humble' is a wrong grammar fact and clashes with expl_pt.

こんにちは is the canonical dictionary kana form; こんにちわ is a recognized misspelling. Pronunciation is carried by romaji and stated in the expl.

findings.issue: を is the object marker here, but the literal renders クッキーを with the topic device 'As for...', misteaching を as if it were は. The expl and tokens correctly call クッキー the object; the literal contradicts them.

notes: Corpus-wide convention: 'As for X' fronts any initial NP, not just は (491/2296 uses have no は; e.g. ビールをなんばい飲みましたか -> 'As for beer...'). expl/tokens teach を correctly.
Batch reserves 'As for' for は (cf. 3501339 lit_en); using it for object を contradicts this record's own expl/tokens.

findings.issue: 'Quanto a...' is the corpus device for the topic particle は, but the particle here is object を; the literal misrepresents the structure (expl/tokens correctly treat クッキー as objeto marcado por を).

'Quanto a' is the batch device for は (cf. 3506554 lit_pt 'quanto a isso'); を is the object marker here.

findings.issue: Particle を left as を; the corpus phonetic convention writes particles as pronounced (を→お), as applied to は→わ elsewhere in this batch. Inconsistent with the convention.

findings.issue: ちょっといいですか？ is a polite permission question ('do you have a moment?'); 'Let me speak.' turns it into a command-like statement, contradicting the record's own expl ('may I speak?') and the pt ('Posso falar um instante?').

'Let me speak.' drops the question and inverts register; record's own expl ('may I speak?') and pt are questions.

findings.issue: 嘘などつくもんか is an indignant rhetorical denial (もんか, the sentence's grammar target). 'I won't lie.' reads as a plain statement of intent — and colloquially as the English hedge 'to be honest' — losing the emphatic force that pt and lit_en render correctly.

'I won't lie.' is propositionally correct; the もんか force is carried by lit_en, pt and expl. Weakening, not a defect.

'He' contradicts en/pt/expl/lit_pt (first person) and 'should have' reads deontic, not epistemic はず.

findings.issue: The grammar target はずだ (speaker's conviction, per expl) is dropped from the natural pt, which reads as a plain past statement. The sibling sentence sent:tatoeba-3552032 renders it ('Eu tenho certeza de que disse...'); this one should too.

findings.issue: いる is misanalyzed as the animate-existence verb (がいる pattern). With inanimate ピザ it must be 要る 'to need/want': ピザがいる人 = 'person who wants/needs pizza' (cf. en 'who wants pizza?'). Existential いる cannot take ピザ as subject; the 'person for whom there is pizza' reading is false grammar.
findings.current: uses the target pattern がいる to indicate the existence of a person: 'ピザがいる人' = 'the person for whom there is pizza / who wants pizza'
findings.suggested: Here いる is 要る ('to need/want'), not existential いる (animate-only): ピザがいる人 = 'person who needs/wants pizza'.
findings.fix: Here いる is 要る ('to need/want'), not existential いる (animate-only): ピザがいる人 = 'person who needs/wants pizza'.
notes: Inanimate ピザ cannot be subject of existential いる; ピザがいる人 = 要る 'needs/wants pizza' (cf. en 'who wants pizza?'). Teaches a false rule.
Inanimate ピザ cannot be subject of animate-existence いる; ピザがいる人 = 要る 'person who needs/wants pizza'. Explanation teaches a false rule.

findings.suggested: Aqui いる é 要る ('precisar/querer'), não o いる de existência (só para seres vivos): ピザがいる人 = 'pessoa que precisa/quer pizza'.

Mesmo erro do expl_en: いる aqui é 要る ('precisar'), não o いる de existência para seres vivos.

findings.issue: Gloss gives the animate-existence sense of いる, which is impossible with inanimate ピザ; in context the verb is 要る 'to need/want'.

findings.issue: Sense inversion: ～ないほうがいい means 'the not-doing side is good' (better NOT to do it), and じゃないかな is only a softening tag. 'It's no good not doing it' attaches the negation to 'good' and advises the opposite of the Japanese.

findings.suggested: The side of not doing it that way is good, isn't it, I wonder?
findings.fix: The side of not doing it that way is good, isn't it, I wonder?
notes: Sense inversion: ないほうがいい advises NOT doing it; 'It's no good not doing it this way' advises the opposite and contradicts en 'you'd better not do that'.
'It's no good not doing it this way' advises the opposite of ～ないほうがいい; polarity inversion in a learner-facing literal.

findings.issue: The negation of the tag じゃない is wrongly prefixed to the ほうがいい block ('não-lado-de-ser-bom' = 'não é bom'), garbling/inverting the structure; the 'good' predicate is affirmative, only the tag is negative.

'não-lado-de-ser-bom' prefixes a negation onto いい and duplicates the じゃない tag already rendered by 'não é mesmo'; garbles polarity.

findings.issue: Wrong person: the sentence is self-directed regret (～ばよかったなあ; en 'I should have come', expl says speaker regret), but lit_en renders it as 'if you'd come', contradicting every other field.

findings.issue: 'Don't go up, will you?' reads in English as a prohibition + tag (request NOT to go up), but お上がりになりませんか is a negative-question invitation ('won't you go up/come in?').

'Don't go up, will you?' reads as prohibition in English; ～ませんか is an invitation. Illocutionary force reversed.

findings.issue: 'has (wants) pizza' carries over the wrong existential/possession reading; 要る means 'to need', as the lit_pt correctly renders ('precisa de').

findings.issue: 'without だ' is misleading after a verb: だ can never follow みる, so the remark implies a nonexistent option. Should say plain (non-polite) form instead.

findings.issue: Same as expl_en: 'sem だ' sugere que だ poderia seguir o verbo みる, o que é agramatical; deve dizer forma simples/sem polidez.

findings.issue: Object particle を left as を instead of the corpus phonetic convention お (は→わ, へ→え, を→お); the romaji already uses 'o' (kuchio...). Inconsistent with the rest of the bank.

findings.issue: それ is the medial demonstrative 'that/it'; 'this' corresponds to これ and is wrong in a gloss for それ (a distinction the course teaches).

findings.issue: Kana is the phonetic field; per the corpus は→わ convention the greeting's final は (historically the topic particle, pronounced わ) should surface as わ. Same fix applies to tokens[0].r.

notes: こんにちは is the standard kana spelling/reading; the は→わ rule applies to particle tokens, not to a lexicalized interjection. こんにちわ would teach a misspelling.
こんにちは is the correct standard kana spelling of a lexicalized word (not a live particle); こんにちわ would teach a misspelling. Romaji already carries pronunciation.
